findings.issue: The BB blind-defence-early justification says the hand re-raises with 'Jacks or better, ace-king and ace-queen suited', and then says 'offsuit aces down to ace-nine' call. In the grid AKo is R (row K, column A; raise 3.3% = AA KK QQ JJ AKs AQs AKo = 44 combos). So the text puts AKo in a call group although it raises. That breaks SPEC-04 'every hand or group named under an action has that action'.
findings.evidence: chart:print 6-max: 'K    R    R    C ...' (AKo R, KK R, KQs C). Why: '... Jacks or better, ace-king and ace-queen suited re-raise. ... offsuit aces down to ace-nine ... call'.
findings.fix: Text only, grid unchanged: 'Jacks or better, ace-king, ace-queen suited and ace-king offsuit re-raise.' and '... offsuit aces from ace-queen down to ace-nine ...'.

findings.issue: This is the same text and grid mismatch as in six-max. The full-ring BB blind-defence-early grid raises AKo (row K, column A = R; raise 3.3%), but the text names only 'ace-king and ace-queen suited' as re-raises, and it puts AKo in the call group 'offsuit aces down to ace-nine'.
findings.evidence: chart:print full-ring: 'K    R    R    C    C ...'. Why: 'Jacks or better, ace-king and ace-queen suited re-raise. ... offsuit aces down to ace-nine ...'.
findings.fix: Text only: say AKo re-raises, and start the offsuit-ace call group at ace-queen.

findings.issue: The chart-level text says 'a raiser in the four earliest seats than against a later one'. At 10 seats there are 5 early seats (two UTG, UTG+1, MP, LJ), so an LJ raiser is the fifth-earliest seat, which the text calls 'later', yet it routes to the early spot. At 8 seats the four earliest seats include HJ, which routes late. The SB early text (line 970, 'the four earliest seats at a full table') has a weaker form of the same problem. In six-max.json:610/630, 'the two earliest seats' is not true at 7 seats either. The spot texts do name the positions, so this is minor.
findings.evidence: EARLY_RAISERS['full-ring'] = UTG, UTG+1, MP, LJ; positionOf maps both 10-seat UTG seats to UTG (route F8).
findings.fix: Name the positions instead of counting seats, e.g. 'against a raiser from under the gun to the lojack'. Drop or soften 'the four/two earliest seats' in the early spot texts.

findings.issue: The raiser's seat is read through `(records[raiseAt] as (typeof records)[number]).seat`. The cast is harder to read than it needs to be.
findings.evidence: raiseAt comes from findIndex on a list that is known to hold one raise.
findings.fix: Optionally use `const raise = records[raiseAt] as PlayerAction` or `records.find(a => a.type === 'raise')`, held in a named local.

summary: Routing is correct for every route group I checked. For seats: both UTG seats at 10 seats map to UTG (early), the earliest seat at 8 seats is UTG+1 (early), the earliest at 5 seats is HJ (early), and 3-4 seats map to CO/BTN (late). For actions: an isolation raise is grouped by the raiser's seat, limps and calls don't count, an SB raiser and a BB raise after the SB completes are late, and heads-up is unchanged. The new test runs 23 routes x 169 classes and would fail under a raiser-blind implementation. Its rule 5/6 checks have a working mutation case. The Rock F1 check can fail because K9s is in the Rock late BB range but not in the early range. The chart:print blocks for all 8 spots match signoff.md line for line. The late grids are unchanged (D-5). Every locked re-pin replaces expected values only and keeps its check count, and each has unlock entries for every owner. The seeded re-pins follow the A-8 method and their u thresholds hold. The new acceptance file passes. One substantive problem: both BB blind-defence-early justifications leave AKo out of the re-raise list and put it in 'offsuit aces down to ace-nine' call, but the grid raises it (SPEC-04). The fix is text only.
